changes.location: Axiom a, prose: action letter after par
changes.evidence: A broad closed oval is crossed by a level bar that extends to its left. Its height and barred-oval form do not securely distinguish upper-case Theta from the writer's lower-case theta. The first occurrence retains the case doubt; later occurrences were inspected separately.

changes.location: Axiom a, prose: cancelled small mark after the action letter
changes.evidence: The small blackened mark has two opposed bends and crossing/retraced strokes; a separate live comma follows. The bends favour a cancelled s, but a heavily cancelled comma remains possible. The cancellation is distinct from the live comma.

changes.location: Axiom a, prose: punctuation after int
changes.evidence: The crossed final t is followed by two vertically separated points forming the colon. There is no separate full stop between t and that colon. The point after aut. is independently present.

changes.location: Axiom a, display: action letter
changes.evidence: This occurrence is a tall oval, slightly open at the upper left, with an interior horizontal stroke. It independently admits the same Theta/theta case ambiguity as the prose occurrence; the first-candidate form is used here under the recurring-glyph convention.

changes.location: Axiom b, display: action letter
changes.evidence: This occurrence has a broader oval and a transverse bar extending left. It was read independently and shares the unresolved case distinction; it is not inferred from axiom a.

changes.location: Axiom b, display: dot immediately after d
changes.evidence: A small detached dark round point lies at the foot of d, before the inner opening parenthesis. Both the inner pair around x_1 and the outer closing parenthesis are separately visible.

changes.location: Consequences, first physical line: invariant at the right copy edge
changes.evidence: The beginning invar- and the compressed remaining strokes are visible; at the edge the final t retains its upright and leftward cross-stroke. The crop resolves the word despite the clipped right side of that final stroke.

changes.location: Consequences, parenthesis after donc: Coker/CoKer
changes.evidence: The open C and o are followed by a tall stem with retraced branching strokes, then the low er ending. The final word is recoverable, but the overwritten internal k does not securely determine its case. No earlier complete word can be isolated beneath it. H's note about overloading is not an uncertainty mark.

changes.location: Consequences, first pi after Coker d =
changes.evidence: A detached roof spans two short downward strokes; a small closed oval stands lower at the right. The index is clearly 0. The barred two-stem letter remains case-ambiguous, with lower-case pi preferred. Every later pi was independently read and its index checked.

changes.location: Name before -Sinh: final vowel in Postnikoff
changes.evidence: The initial P, compressed ostn, dotted i, tall k and two long f descenders are visible. The low stroke between k and ff is not a securely closed o and can also be read u. The crop does not justify removing C's doubt.

changes.location: Joining stroke between the two physical lines Postnikoff- and Sinh
changes.evidence: One short horizontal joining dash is present after the two f descenders at the right edge. Sinh begins the next physical line. The crop covers the line-end stroke; half a supplies the independently read next-line word.

changes.location: Cohomology display: isolated point after membership sign
changes.evidence: There is a small separate round dark point low between the membership sign and H. It is appreciably smaller than the final sentence point. Its existence is clear, but it could be either an intentional pen point or a copying/surface speck; intentional status remains uncertain.

changes.location: Lower prose, third physical line: je ne vais pas te
changes.evidence: The first letter is a low shallow v with a rising right hook, followed by a, a dotted i, and the separate curved final s. Its first stroke differs from the two-bend form of the final s.

changes.location: Lower prose, after d'ailleurs de: retomber
changes.evidence: The opening r is heavily retraced and crossed by its outgoing stroke; e, tall t, looped o, low m, angular b and the final er are distinguishable. The word is live. No separate earlier word is legible in the initial retracing.

changes.location: Lower prose, new physical line before un corps parfait: sur
changes.evidence: The dark initial s has a diagonal return and lower bend; the joined u and final r shoulder follow on the same baseline. The word sur is recoverable despite the crowded initial strokes.

changes.location: Alleged separate deleted word before sur, across the physical line break
changes.evidence: The crop shows one crowded group, sur, at the new line's start, without a separate preceding word or a distinct strike across such a word. Half b also shows no extra cancelled group after the closing quotes of ordinaires on the preceding line. Retracing within sur does not permit recovery or secure assertion of an additional deleted word. The two source boxes cover both sides of the alleged line-break locus; the crop covers only the second.

changes.location: Lower prose: accent of algébriques
changes.evidence: A short detached stroke above the e immediately after g is nearly vertical and appears to lean down to the right, favouring a grave accent. Its short, thick form leaves an acute reading possible. All letters of the word are otherwise legible. The long low stroke beneath alg- is continuous with the g descender, not a separate underline.

changes.location: Lower prose: punctuation immediately after underlined affines
changes.evidence: A low hooked punctuation stroke stands beyond the final s and separately from the underline. Enlargement also shows a small higher detached point. A comma with a broken head/tail is preferred, but a semicolon cannot be excluded. H omits the punctuation altogether.

changes.location: Lower prose: quotation pair around ordinaires
changes.evidence: Each end consists of two short raised pen strokes. No angular guillemets are drawn. This records the ink shape even if H's guillemets are house typography.

changes.location: Final physical line: opening quotation before le caractère
changes.evidence: Two raised short strokes precede le. They are double quotation marks, not an angular opening guillemet. No closing pair is present on this page.

changes.location: Final word of the page
changes.evidence: The final group has a low d loop with an upright, then the shallow u shoulder and a long outgoing stroke that hooks at the edge. There is no separately formed e followed by an s. The line continues beyond this page without an added closing quote.

notes: Author claims: a) d commutes with the stated L_0 operations; the displayed equality is transcribed as written. b) the action letter applied to d.(x_1) equals int(x_1). These are author assertions, not proofs supplied or checked by this reader.

Author claims: Im d is invariant in L_0, its cokernel defines pi_0, Ker d = pi_1 is central in L_1, and L_0 acts while preserving pi_1 and acts via pi_0. The unusual wording en invariant and the antecedent of qu'il opère via are preserved, without grammatical or mathematical repair.

Author claims: the principal cohomological invariant is the named Postnikoff/Postnikuff-Sinh invariant alpha in H^3(pi_0,pi_1). The inserted coh. and the small possible point after the membership sign are both retained in their distinct states.

The lower paragraph reports encountering these structures in several situations and mentions ordinary formal groups over a perfect field, affine algebraic groups, commutative formal groups and strict Gr-structures. The marginal note refers to the same formalism on an arbitrary topos, not only (Ens). It has no secure word-level insertion anchor.

The manuscript author number is 5. The separate pencil archive number is 150 and appears only as a comment. No date, salutation, closing or signature occurs on this continuation page. The final quotation and parenthesis remain open at the page end, as written.
No explicit authorial doubt expression occurs on this page. The transcription doubt marks are reader judgments; évidemment is an authorial assertion, not evidence that an uncertain glyph is settled.

Visual prompts: case of each action letter and each pi, all 0/1 indices, both point placements in the axioms, both levels of parentheses in b, the exponent 3, the Im/Ker/Coker letters, the possible point after membership, and every marginal Ens bracket were individually inspected. Expected mathematics was not used to repair the ink.

The higher point after affines and the near-vertical accent in algébriques were assessed in the already-required accent crop; no redundant new crop was made. Their intentional reading remains uncertain where shown.

No OCR, external sources, other pages, other readers, main decisions, delegation, LaTeX compilation or mathematical verification were used. checks is empty because the work was visual transcription, not one of the six mathematical check-event types.

coverage: The whole image was viewed once for layout, then half a and half b were viewed once each in that order. Every physical body line listed in line_coverage was read against both complete witnesses, including their agreed text, accents, endings and punctuation. The two axioms and the cohomology display were read symbol by symbol; each occurrence of the action letter, pi, x, L, its index, the exponent, the parentheses and the equality signs was separately inspected. The cancellation after the first action letter, overtraced Coker/retomber/sur strokes, inserted coh., two underlines, quotation marks, whole sideways note, depleted marginal line, its guide and both page numbers were inventoried. Sixteen tight crops were made by the prescribed script and each was viewed once; no whole half was enlarged again. C's ten distinct doubt/unreadability loci all have resolution or retention entries. H omits the cancelled small sign, the dot after d in b, the possible point after membership and the punctuation after affines; it also differs in vais, du and the marginal ce. Its claimed separate deleted word before sur is not securely present in this scan. The faint marginal line is acknowledged in H's note and is not falsely counted as an H omission. H's page-number note, operator macro syntax and emphasis macro syntax are not treated as omissions or wording differences. The report preserves uncertainty rather than importing H's explanation based on a different facsimile.
